Potter Cove Body Mass and Biomass Dataset

Source: R/data.r
PotterCove_bm.Rd

This dataset contains curated body mass, biomass, and resource density information for consumers and resources in the Potter Cove food web, from Rodriguez & Saravia (2024). The dataset was processed from raw measurements, with units converted to kilograms (kg), and some special handling for detritus and sponge taxa where direct body mass or density values were not available or meaningful.

Usage

PotterCove_bm

Format

A data frame with the following columns:

consumer

Name of the consumer species.

resource

Name of the resource species.

c_bodymass

Body mass of the consumer (in kg).

r_bodymass

Body mass of the resource (in kg). May be set to 1 for detritus or sponges.

r_biomass

Biomass of the resource (in kg).

r_density

Resource density (units depend on context). May be 1 for some resources or -999 to flag missing values.

Source

https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10790590

Details

When resource density is unknown, the value -999 is used as a flag so that downstream functions can infer density or body mass using allometric relationships following Pawar et al. (2012). Body mass and biomass were originally in grams and converted to kilograms. Sponge taxa (e.g., Chalinidae, Dendrilla antarctica) resource body mass and density were assigned to 1.

References

Rodriguez, I. D., & Saravia, L. A. (2024). Potter Cove’s Heavyweights: Estimation of Species’ Interaction Strength of an Antarctic Food Web. Ecology and Evolution, 14(11), e70389. https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.70389

Pawar, S., Dell, A.I., & Savage, V.M. (2012). Dimensionality of consumer search space drives trophic interaction strengths. Nature, 486(7404), 485–489.
